questions.q: What is the total mass of the solution when 1 gram of salt is dissolved in 20 grams of water?
questions.note: Mass is conserved: solute + solvent = 1 + 20 = 21 g.

questions.q: A salt solution can be made more concentrated by boiling off some of the water. Which statement is true about the solution after this process?
opts: The amount of solute remains the same but the amount of solvent decreases.
The amount of solute and the amount of solvent increase.
The amount of solute and the amount of solvent decrease.
The amount of solute remains the same but the amount of solvent increases.
The amount of solvent remains the same but the amount of solute decreases.

questions.q: The amount of solute in each of the beakers shown below is represented by the number of black dots. The volume is shown on the side. In which beaker does the solute have the smallest concentration?
opts: More than one has the same smallest concentration
questions.given: HINT: Count each dot as 1 mol. You should calculate a few to make sure.
questions.note: Dots ÷ mL: Beaker 1: 8/10 = 0.8, Beaker 2: 6/10 = 0.6, Beaker 3: 6/15 = 0.4, Beaker 4: 12/20 = 0.6. Beaker 3 is lowest.

questions.q: There are different ways of representing molarity. Select all the answers that represent a 1.0 molarity solution.
opts: 1.0 moles popping out of a tunnel
questions.note: Molarity is mol solute per L solution, written M, "molar", or with square brackets. Molality is a different unit.

questions.q: Solute, Solvent, Solution, Saturation — review the Molarity Defined and Molarity Calculations pages.
What is the molarity of a solution of potassium bromide if 4.50 moles is dissolved in enough water to make 0.750 L of solution?
What is the molarity of a solution if 42.7 moles is dissolved in enough water to make 7.7 L of solution?
questions.given: Record your answer with the correct number of significant figures.
questions.note: 42.7 ÷ 7.7 = 5.545. 7.7 L has two sig figs, so 5.5 M.

questions.q: A student planned to evaporate a solution so that there was only solid left. They wanted to collect 1.19 g of sodium fluoride (NaF molar mass = 41.99 g/mol). What volume (in mL) of 0.945 M NaF solution need to be in the flask to generate the expected amount of NaF?
questions.given: Be careful to pay attention to the units and report your answer with the correct number of significant figures!
questions.note: 1.19 ÷ 41.99 = 0.02834 mol. ÷ 0.945 M = 0.02999 L. eLearn accepted 29.9 mL; strict rounding gives 30.0 mL, so both count here.

questions.q: If a substance is diluted, what characteristics would you expect?
opts: The solution will either have more volume or less solute.
The solution will have a darker vibrant color.
The numerical value of the molarity will go down.
If it is being created from a concentrated solution, the concentrated solution is put in a volumetric flask and then water is added so that it fills the entire flask to the very top.
questions.note: A diluted solution is lighter in color, and you fill to the graduation line, not the very top.

questions.q: When doing dilution calculations, why should the volume units be the same value?
opts: So that the unit will cancel.
So that you know everything will fit in the any flask
So that the dilution is faster in the lab.
